quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help a rider become more visible?

options.text: Using the headlight at all times

questions.explanation: To be visible to other drivers, wear bright clothing with reflective materials, use your headlight at all times, and use your turn signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: What should passengers do?

options.text: Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean as the operator leans. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator, and hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Move as far to the right as possible to help them.
Move to the shoulder to help them.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center portion of your lane. Riding on either side increases the risk of a crash. The passing driver might merge back into your lane too soon if you ride too far to the right.

questions.question: Where is the horn button usually located?
questions.explanation: Know the location of all your motorcycle's controls before you ride. The horn button is usually located next to the left handgrip.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to operate any motor vehicle while intoxicated.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: Hand signals can be used instead of or in addition to turn signals. When the operator's left arm is bent at the elbow and points downward, it means the operator will slow down or stop.

questions.question: Shifting into a lower gear has an effect similar to:
questions.explanation: Shifting into a lower gear slows your motorcycle, similar to applying the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After at least an hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes occur on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts riding.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another vehicle on the left, you should:

options.text: Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
Not signal your intentions, as that may distract the driver you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When passing on the left, ride in the left portion of your lane. Signal before you pass and check for traffic. Pass when it is safe, then signal and return to your original lane.

questions.question: Successful motorcycle riders are safest when they are:

options.text: On the side of the road.
In the left side of the lane.

questions.explanation: Successful motorcycle riders are safest when other drivers can clearly see them. Use your headlight, brake light, signals, and lane position to be more visible.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Ride in the part of the lane that makes other drivers see you as early as possible.
Always be in the left lane to stay away from oncoming traffic.
Slowly sneak up to the intersection.
Weave slightly in your lane so your headlight is spotted better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the part of the lane that makes other drivers see you as early as possible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the part of your lane where oncoming drivers will see you sooner. For example, if you are approaching a blind corner on your right, ride in the left part of your lane instead of the center.

questions.question: Before you get on your motorcycle, your pre-ride check should include everything except:
questions.explanation: Your pre-ride check should include tires, oil and fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn. Do a full check before every ride.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best way to stay close while keeping safe distance is to ride:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets you stay close to the group while keeping enough space for safety. Use single-file when riding on curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side with another rider.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire going flat. Tire failure usually shows itself by a change in how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should keep you out of other vehicles' blind spots, help you see and be seen, help you avoid surface hazards, help you avoid wind blasts, and give you an escape route. Position yourself to discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because:

options.text: The front tire powers the bike, so you lose acceleration.
The flat tire shakes the bike, making it hard to use the mirrors.
You won't be able to use the brake.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because it affects your steering. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely get off the road as quickly as possible.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Does not mean the driver will properly yield to you.
Guarantees the driver will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean the driver will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to ensure a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists and still do not see them.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, such as speed limit signs, are rectangular with white background and black lettering or symbols. Follow all rules posted on these signs.

questions.question: A person is considered legally intoxicated when their blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is at least ______.
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means a person is legally intoxicated. Driving under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If one rider in a group wants to go faster than the others, what should the group do?

options.text: Let that rider go ahead and meet up at a planned location later.
Speed up to keep up with that rider.
Split up and let each rider go at their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let that rider go ahead and meet up at a planned location later.
questions.explanation: If one group member wants to ride faster, let them go ahead. The group should meet at a planned spot later.

questions.question: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles helps because:

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You will have a narrower view and stay more focused.
You will have more time to react to what other vehicles do.
You can more easily follow the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to react to what other vehicles do.
questions.explanation: Space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you a clearer view of hazards, more time to react, and more room to maneuver safely.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to handle differently while riding, you should:

options.text: Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over and check the chain.
Pull over and check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A change in how your motorcycle handles may mean a tire has failed. Pull over safely and check your tires.

questions.question: A motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Can tip over if you turn too fast.
Can take corners at any speed.
Should not carry any loaded items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can tip over if you turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Even with three wheels, a sidecar can tip over if you turn too sharply or go too fast around a corner.
